FACT: claimDirectiveDispatch() transitions only PENDING/ENQUEUED to PROCESSING and returns BUSY whenever it reads PROCESSING.
reconcilePendingDispatches() selects PENDING/ENQUEUED plus policy-authorized FAILED rows; PROCESSING is not selected for reconciliation.

The worker calls claimDirectiveDispatch() before SWARM execution. A process termination after the durable PROCESSING claim and before completeDirectiveDispatch()/failDirectiveDispatch() can therefore leave the row PROCESSING without that process running its failure callback.
On a later delivery of the same BullMQ job, claimDirectiveDispatch() returns BUSY for the still-PROCESSING row.
processJob() converts BUSY to a normal JobState.CANCELLED return with commandResult='Dispatch already processing', so that delivery does not reclaim or execute the run.
The exact Test-AI worker registers completed/error/failed listeners but no repository-owned stalled/reclaim handler was found.
The existing queue restart reconciliation proof exercises a PENDING dispatch, not a crash after durable PROCESSING claim.
UNKNOWN: This audit did not execute a real process-kill/BullMQ stalled-job recovery scenario; exact BullMQ retry timing and max-stalled behavior are not claimed.

The final repair mechanism is not prescribed. Lease/heartbeat, generation-token CAS, explicit crash-reclaim, or another evidence-backed design may satisfy recovery if it preserves exactly-once authority and fail-closed release.
EXPECTED: A worker/process crash after a durable claim must not leave required work permanently unrecoverable in PROCESSING.
Recovery must not allow two workers to execute the same authoritative run concurrently or duplicate final LAW-authorized output.
A redelivery for an abandoned processing claim must have an explicit durable recovery decision rather than being silently normalized to BUSY/CANCELLED forever.
The recovery path must remain deterministic/evidence-backed and must not introduce host-clock authority unless active authority explicitly permits it.

AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE.ACTIVE_SCOPE: Final DOC-C includes queue + idempotency in required build scope and defines canonical queue defaults.
AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE.V8_CLOSURE: V8 requires REPLAY, PERSISTENCE, RECOVERY, CONCURRENCY and error-path verification and treats REPLAY_DEFECT / UNHANDLED_REQUIRED_STATE / DATA_INTEGRITY_DEFECT as actionable gaps.
AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE.NON_CLAIM: Final DOC-C was not found to mandate a specific PROCESSING lease/heartbeat algorithm.

SOURCE_EVIDENCE.E2E_LIMITATION: Restart reconciliation creates/reconciles a pending dispatch; it does not kill a worker after PROCESSING claim.

REPRODUCTION_MODEL: Start with durable DirectiveDispatch=ENQUEUED and a valid BullMQ job.
Worker W claims it, atomically changing durable state to PROCESSING.
Terminate W before it reaches success/failure persistence.
No W callback can change the durable row after process death.
A subsequent delivery invokes claimDirectiveDispatch and reads PROCESSING -> BUSY.
Current processJob returns CANCELLED/Dispatch already processing without executing the pipeline or recovering durable state.
The periodic reconciler does not select PROCESSING, so repository-owned recovery is absent in the inspected code.
